newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says agglomerated grated cheese still grated cheese.
newsitem.headline: Court says agglomerated grated cheese still grated cheese.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Tuesday that grated cheese, even in an agglomerated form for shipping, remains under the customs classification for grated and powdered cheese.
The agglomerated cheese in question in the case pending before a Portuguese court breaks down into irregular granules once exposed to air, the court said,

"The court has consistently held that, in the interests of legal certainty and ease of verification, the decisive criterion for the customs classification of goods must be their objective characteristics and properties, as defined by the wording of the headings of the Common Customs Tariff and the notes to the sections of chapters," the judgment said.
The heading under review in this judgment was "cheese and curd" and the court found grated cheese, even in an agglomerated form during shipping, fell under that category.
Reference to the court by the Supremo Tribunal Administrativo for a preliminary ruling pending before that court between
Fabrica de Queijo Eru Portuguesa Ld
Alfandega de Lisboa (Tribunal Tecnico Aduaneiro de 2e Instancia)

on the interpretation of subheadings 0406 20 90 and 0406 90 11 of Council regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 on the Common Customs Tariff (OJ 1987 L 256, p. 1) as amended, and by Commission regulation (EEC) No 316/91 concerning the classification of certain goods in the combined nomenclature (OJ 1991 L 37, p. 25)

Subheading 0406 20 90 of Council regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 on the Common Customs Tariff, as amended must be interpreted as including grated cheese which, when imported, is, by reason of the method of packaging and preservation used, in an agglomerated form and, after unpacking and exposure to the surrounding air, breaks down into irregular granules.
